newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Old Mutual funnels cash to fixed income.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Old Mutual funnels cash to fixed income.

text.p: South Africa's leading life assurer, Old Mutual, said on Monday it tripled fixed income investment in the year to June 30 while equity investments fell by 26 percent.

Group cash flow invested in equities fell to 3.270 billion rand from 4.428 billion in the previous year while cash applied to interest-bearing stocks, debentures and other loans jumped to 6.099 billion from 2.040 billion, the company said.
Chairman Mike Levett told Reuters the trend towards fixed income investments had continued in the first part of the current year.

Despite this, the group's balance sheet showed equities remained the group's dominant asset group, rising to 106.74 billion rand from 77.84 billion at June 30, 1995, reflecting price gains on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Fixed income investments stood at 38.87 billion rand against 30.65 billion.

Within the equity portfolio, mining producers accounted for 12.25 billion rand, mining financials 12.84 billion, banks, insurers and financial services 22.02 billion, industrials 48.31 billion and equity trusts 11.32 billion.
Announcing year results earlier, Old Mutual said total assets under management had increased by 28 percent to 198.1 billion rand in the financial year to June 30.
